_purpose: Orchestrator continuity across Claude Code sessions. The HUMAN talks to ONE AI (the orchestrator); that AI dispatches scope-specific work via the Agent tool. When the human starts a fresh Claude Code session, the new orchestrator MUST read this file early in startup so it knows: what was last being worked on, what's pending, what decisions were just made, what scopes are currently claimed, what to NOT re-do.
_protocol: Update this file at every significant decision/checkpoint. Treat it like a running session journal — newest at the bottom of recent_decisions, oldest pruned. The aggregator script `node scripts/agent-status.js` complements this with per-scope status from data/coordination/sessions/*.json.
_what_vs_why: As of v0.283.x: this file records WHY decisions were made (running journal). `docs/PRIORITIES.md` records WHAT comes next (strict-ranked backlog). Both must be updated when scope changes. Don't put 'next action' here — put it in PRIORITIES.md.

recent_decisions.decision: Fluids as litres, first rung (v0.1347.0): data/containers/fluids.ron names tap-water items (water_purified_0 = 1 L) and carryable vessels (bottle 0.5 L, jerrycan 20 L). Crafting draws tap water from the tanks when the pack lacks it (manual and auto paths; refused and nothing spent when the tanks are low); the Crafting page counts the tanks. A water tank card fills and pours vessels. Drinking a bottle returns the empty bottle.
recent_decisions.why: The tanks held real litres and the water items came from nowhere; this joins the two. A vessel is an empty item plus a full item because ItemStack carries no metadata and real vessels keep to one fluid anyway (a water jerrycan is never a fuel can). No auto recipe uses water, so automation cannot drain the cistern. Tests red on purpose first.

recent_decisions.decision: Crafting depth rung 1 (v0.1348.0): hand tools. data/crafting/tools.ron (rules by station+category, per-recipe overrides) gives 182 recipes tools that must be in the backpack; not consumed; ItemStack gained a serde-default wear counter and Inventory::wear_item breaks one at items.csv durability. Automated machines need no tools; creative skips the check. Starter kit + hammer, hand saw, screwdriver, wrench, pliers. Statues stopped consuming their chisel. The web recipes.json generator resolves the same tools and a Rust test compares every recipe across the two.
recent_decisions.why: Operator-agreed gameplay order item 5 (crafting depth). Tools-as-items is the real model and ItemStack was only ever built via ItemStack::new, so per-stack wear was a clean add. The obtainability test (fixed point over vendor, kit and recipes) exists because a rule can silently lock recipes behind a tool nobody can get: it failed on purpose with forge_hammer_0, which has no source. Tests red on purpose first. Gardening rung 1 (yield from health, six unmapped plant model sets) was handed to a worktree agent in parallel.

recent_decisions.decision: Crafting depth rung 2 (v0.1349.0): station power. MachinePower::Consumer gained idle_watts (serde default None, skipped when None so editor saves do not churn); machine entities carry MachineType; a StationLoad component holds active/idle watts and the crafting tick sets PowerConsumer.draw_watts to active while a craft runs at the station (auto: its own batch; manual: one powered station of the type), idle otherwise. A manual craft at an electric station with no powered machine of its type is refused with a notice; the Crafting page mirrors it via GuiState.unpowered_station_types. Family home: stove idle 0, oven 2, electronics bench 5, sewing machine 0.
recent_decisions.why: Those four drew ~3.65 kW around the clock, which is not how a stove works and distorted the home power budget. Not done: pausing a running craft when power drops (rung 3). An idle 0 W consumer is disabled by the shedder on an over-budget island, which reads as no power, and that is intended: there is no spare power to switch it on. Tests red on purpose first (no gate; no drop to idle).
